facts.statement: Researchers collected the fossil remains of Khinganornis in May 2017 at the Pigeon Hill locality.
facts.quote: In May 2017, following fieldwork efforts at the Pigeon Hill locality, researchers collected the remains of an ornithuromorph bird.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen is housed at Hebei Geo University under the accession number SGM-AVE-2017001.
facts.quote: The specimen is housed at Hebei Geo University, where it is permanently accessioned as specimen SGM-AVE-2017001.

facts.statement: Khinganornis lived during the Aptian age of the Early Cretaceous in Inner Mongolia, China.
facts.quote: Khinganornis is an extinct genus of euornithean bird from the Early Cretaceous (Aptian age) Longjiang Formation of Inner Mongolia, China.

facts.statement: The species lived between 121.4 and 113.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Aptian to Aptian (121.4 to 113.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: Khinganornis had elongated toes and lower legs similar to modern amphibious or wading birds.
facts.quote: The toes and lower legs of Khinganornis are elongated, similar to modern birds with an amphibious or wading ecology.

facts.statement: The bird possessed blunt, low-crowned teeth in its upper and lower jaws.
facts.quote: It has blunt, low-crowned teeth in the maxilla and dentary (upper and lower jaws), with those in the premaxilla being smaller but similar in shape.

facts.statement: An ossified predentary bone was present at the tip of the lower jaw.
facts.quote: An ossified predentary is present at the tip of the dentary.

facts.statement: The pubis bone was slender and longer than the femur.
facts.quote: The pubis is slender and longer than the femur.

facts.statement: The leg bones were arranged with the tarsometatarsus being the longest, followed by the tibiotarsus, then the femur.
facts.quote: The tarsometatarsus is longer than the tibiotarsus, which is longer than the femur.

facts.statement: Its leg proportions and ankle structure suggest a semiaquatic ecology similar to modern wading birds.
facts.quote: These proportions, in addition to the lateral compression of the end of the tarsometatarsus and the high, recessed trochlea II, are similar to modern birds with a semiaquatic ecology.

facts.statement: Based on its close relatives, Khinganornis likely preferred wading in nearshore aquatic environments.
facts.quote: Gansus and Iteravis, two close relatives, have been interpreted as living in coastal or littoral (nearshore) regions, implying Khinganornis also preferred wading in a near-aquatic environment.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analyses classify Khinganornis as a member or close relative of the family Gansuidae.
facts.quote: Phylogenetic analyses place it as a close relative or member of the family Gansuidae.

facts.statement: The genus is classified within the family Gansuidae.
It is debated how Khinganornis relates to other birds, as different phylogenetic methodologies have produced contrasting evolutionary trees.
facts.quote: Wang et al., 2025 (describing Shuilingornis from China's Jiufotang Formation) used an updated version of the original Khinganornis matrix recovered two contrasting tree topologies depending on the methodology used.
